findings.title: Fallback locales are not loaded on the translation path
findings.body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale), while ApplicationController#set_locale is the only caller of I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Code outside a web request, such as background jobs and mailers, and translations using an explicit locale: option can therefore invoke the new Fallbacks backend before the site-default and :en YAML files have been lazily loaded. Those lookups return 'translation missing' instead of falling back; for calls without interpolation arguments, that missing string is also stored frozen in the LRU cache keyed only by key and locale, so it can continue to be served after a later request loads :en until cache eviction or reload. All fallback locales for the effective or explicit locale should be loaded inside translate/lookup before consulting or caching the backend.

findings.title: Custom fallbacks object discards I18n::Locale::Fallbacks behavior
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList inherits directly from Hash and replaces the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks object previously configured by Rails, but its [] ignores anything stored in the hash and the class provides neither Locale::Fallbacks' defaults nor its map configuration API. It also loses parent-tag expansion: for a locale such as en_GB, a missing key is resolved in SiteSetting.default_locale before its parent :en, because :en appears only as the final entry. Existing or plugin code using the documented fallbacks API can therefore be silently ignored or fail, and regional locales can receive the site language instead of their parent language. The custom ordering should be implemented by subclassing or extending I18n::Locale::Fallbacks rather than replacing it with a plain Hash.

findings.title: Every backend lookup now consults SiteSetting
findings.body: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] for every uncached translation, localization, and pluralization lookup, and this implementation calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every such call. That puts the DB-backed settings subsystem on the hot translation path that translate_accelerator otherwise optimizes through lazy loading and caching, and it also makes translations attempted during boot, rake, or asset tasks depend on SiteSetting being loadable before the fallback chain can even be computed. The chain should be cached and invalidated when default_locale changes, rather than recomputed through SiteSetting for each lookup.

findings.title: No tests cover the custom fallback backend or lazy loading
findings.body: This change replaces the Rails fallback configuration with a custom Hash, moves pluralization setup into config/initializers/i18n.rb, removes config.i18n.fallbacks from the environment files, and adds lazy loading of fallback locales, but it adds no specs. Nothing verifies that a key missing from the user locale falls back first to the site default and then to :en, that the relevant locale files are loaded outside ApplicationController, or that pluralized strings obtained through a fallback still use the fallback locale's pluralization rules. Regressions would surface only as wrong-language text or 'translation missing' strings in production.
